text:
mike: ran into a confusing auth failure during onboarding. Rotated a project key, exported REDWOOD_API_KEY, but sample-service still returned 401s.

anya: did you have any other REDWOOD_* envs set or a creds file? quick paste of debug helps.

mike: no REDWOOD_TOKEN set on my shell. There is a `~/.redwood/creds` from earlier experiments. I unset it and restart fixed it, but that's not great. Logs: 
```
2025-04-03T10:02:11Z ERROR POST /v1/generate 401 {"error":"invalid_api_key"}
2025-04-03T10:02:11Z DEBUG credential-resolver: returning token from file ~/.redwood/creds (masked ****abcd)
```

anya: thanks. Sounds like SDK resolver cached the disk token or prioritized file over env. Which SDK/runtime?

mike: node 18 + redwood-sdk-js v1.8.3.

sdk-bot: FYI parity note: older Node resolver prioritized disk file for historical reasons (server daemon patterns). Newer Python SDK treats env as highest priority. We should unify.

ops-rita: production impact note: we saw a dedicated customer hit a similar issue during org key rotation last month. Their autoscaler updated files and then envs, so some pods kept the old creds. Caused 5m of errors.

kate: proposed mitigation: 1) make resolver prefer REDWOOD_API_KEY (env) per-request (cheap check) 2) when changing effective token, invalidate in-memory cache and clear any batchers using the old token 3) emit a clear masked WARNING at startup if env and creds file both exist and differ 4) add a CLI flag `--no-write` so onboarding flows can avoid writing disk creds by default.

mike: small UX ask: can the SDK print which source it used (env/file/cli) on first request (masked)? That would've saved me 10min.

anya: agreed. Also propose adding a background watcher option (opt-in) that watches `process.env` or a sentinel file for changes and reloads creds on SIGHUP. Many apps don't restart on rotation.

ops-rita: for Dedicated customers, our runbook already suggests restarting workers, but we can add a small smoke test: after rotation, call /health or /v1/ping to validate 2 successful requests before cutting traffic. We'll add that to KB.

sdk-bot: actions: file issue redwood/sdk-cred#999 to implement env-first resolution + cache invalidation + masked-source log. Add PR for docs to standardize on REDWOOD_API_KEY in all sampleapps and CLI onboarding.

kate: tests: unit tests for env-only, file-only, file-then-env (rotation while running), env-then-file, and an integration test that simulates container mount of ~/.redwood to catch Docker pitfalls. Also CI job to lint Dockerfiles for COPY of home creds.

mike: temporary workaround I documented in sample-service README: `unset REDWOOD_TOKEN && rm -f ~/.redwood/creds && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=newkey && pkill -HUP -f sample-service || npm run dev`. Not ideal but helps during demos.

anya: long term: central credential-resolver library used by all SDKs so we don't repeat precedence bugs. We'll draft an RFC. Include telemetry event when a request fails with 401 due to token mismatch so support can triage rotations quickly. Mask tokens in telemetry.

kate: I'll take docs + CLI change (add --no-write and a warning when writing creds into common mount locations). ops-rita will update Dedicated runbook. mike please open a repro gist and link to the issue.

mike: done, gist linked in issue #999. Thanks everyone — PR incoming with a minimal change to log the token source on first request (masked) so users can see where auth came from.

sdk-bot: reminder: tag eng-runtime and devex on PRs, include tests, and coordinate release notes for v1.9.0.
